brief: SPX closed at its lowest level since May and VIX continues to overshoot moves in the underlying, with the past three sessions showing little outright panic in spot even as volatility spikes. Markets can trend lower without volatility needing to rise much. VIX sits at 25, VVIX at 121, and stress is most pronounced in tech, where VXN has lagged VIX but the gap stays wide. Skew has ground higher since early October with downside protection well bid and little sign of the crowd monetizing hedges. Nomura puts aggregate SPX dealer gamma near negative $7.3bn, close to the bottom of its range, which can amplify moves in either direction. McElligott sees the VIX floor rising but limited fuel for a shock above 30 without a much deeper selloff. Systematic strategies have already sold $116bn over two weeks, cutting exposure to the 10th percentile and net leverage to near zero, leaving room for a painful upside squeeze if volatility cools. Nomura's model shows a further 5% decline could trigger $81.8bn of mechanical selling, while a 5% rally would imply $66.1bn of buying.
